issue.title: Rerun the second-zero controls with a non-Kummer planted family
issue.body:
**What.** Rerun #203's planted controls with a family that has a non-Kummer singularity, such as a branch point plus a pole, fitted to the σ data to better than 0.1% per coefficient. Recommended by #203's subagent.

**Why.** #203's planted family is a Kummer function that matches each σ_n to 0.2–0.9%. On the real data the approximants spread about 20 times more than on that family, so its accuracy is not an error bar for the real crossing.

**Acceptance (can fail).** A crossing planted at 1.095 is found within 0.005, and one at 1.15 is rejected, through #203's code on ten seeds. Report the spread of the approximants on the new family against the real data's.

**Depends on.** #203.

comments.body: started: coordinator's subagent on the Apple M5 Mac (`mac`), worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-aefe0d5d13e2c2f85` of nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d at 9973e4d, one process under `nice -n 10`. Code extends `solver/independent_second_zero/`, backed up to `wip/i214`. Raw folder `I214-mac/`, whose README will hold the acceptance criteria before any control runs.

Progress (mac, 2026-11-09 03:10 UTC, one process under `nice -n 10`, about 1 of 10 cores, memory < 0.1 GB).

**The family.** A Laplace integral over a curved arc with a non-Beta density, S(x; w) = ∫₀¹ e^{x γ(s)} ρ(s) ds / ∫ρ, where γ(s) = za + s(zp − za) + κ s(1 − s) and ρ(s) = s^{α−1}(1 − s)^{β−1}(e₀ + e₁ s). All seven complex parameters are linear in w, from one joint fit to the three nodes (variable projection). #203's Kummer family is the case κ = 0, e₁ = 0. Its F(t) has a square-root branch point at the critical value of γ, besides the two ends.

**Fit quality**, max over n = 1..22 of |log(σ_model/σ_data)|:

| w | arc | Kummer (#203) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.09 | 9.2e-5 | 8.5e-3 |
| 1.10 | 7.5e-5 | 8.7e-3 |
| 1.11 | 8.4e-5 | 8.9e-3 |

Its Domb–Sykes ζ at n = 20–22 is 1.63 + 1.18i, against the data's 1.64 + 1.19i and the Kummer family's 1.48 + 1.09i.

**The family's own zero**, exact (series at 160 digits, checked against quadrature to 3e-49), is 13.43493 + 0.05484i, 13.50254 − 0.04904i, 13.56897 − 0.15525i at the three nodes. It crosses at w_nat = 1.09531. The real-data estimate is 13.40094 + 0.10383i, ... with a crossing at 1.09884. So matching σ₀..σ₂₂ to 1e-4 leaves x1 free at about 0.04.

**Planting** is by a shift in w, S_p(x; w) = S(x; w − (w_p − w_nat)). P1's shift is −0.0003, and P2's is +0.0547.

The criteria, including the spread-match rule (real/arc spread ratio in 1/3–3 at every node), are in `I214-mac/README.md`, committed before any control ran (raw 7b5efe0). A pilot on a non-control configuration (w_p 1.105, seed 99) passed, with a crossing error of 6e-6. Its primary spread was 1.5e-4 to 4.5e-4 per node, against the data's 7e-4 to 1.3e-3.

P1, P2, the mutations and the information runs are going now (`run_all.sh`, about 1 h). Code: `wip/i214` 895ac75. Raw: `I214-mac/` at 768793c.

Progress (mac, 2026-11-09 03:44 UTC, one process under `nice -n 10`, about 1 of 10 cores, memory < 0.1 GB).

Both controls pass on the arc family, ten seeds each, with 1e-12 relative noise.

| control | verdict | detail |
|---|---|---|
| P1, crossing at 1.095 | pass, 10/10 | primary crossings 1.094990–1.094997, so the error is ≤ 1.0e-5; |x1 error| per node ≤ 1.9e-4 |
| P2, crossing at 1.15 | pass, 10/10 | primary median Im x1 is +0.5823, +0.4909, +0.3973 against the true +0.58234, +0.49098, +0.39736; no sign change; P1's criterion fails on this family, as it must |

The x1 errors on P1 lean the same way at every seed and node, about +5e-5 in Re and −6e-5 in Im. That is a common bias, so it cancels in the crossing.

Next are the mutations M1 (partial sum only) and M2 (crossing planted at 1.105 but tested at 1.095), the information runs at noise 1e-14 and 0, and then the spread comparison. Raw: `I214-mac/` at 78e28e6. Code: `wip/i214` 895ac75.

Progress (mac, 2026-11-09 04:50 UTC, one process under `nice -n 10`, about 1 of 10 cores, memory < 0.1 GB).

**Mutations.** Both fire.
- M1 (partial sum, no continuation) puts the zeros near −3.3 + 5.4i and finds no crossing, so P1 fails. Exit 0.
- M2 (crossing planted at 1.105, tested at 1.095) finds 1.10500, so P1 fails. Exit 1.

**Spread, against the pre-set rule.** It **does not match**. The rule asks that the real/arc ratio of the primary per-node half-ranges (median over the ten P1 seeds) lie in 1/3–3 at every node, in both Re and Im. The ratios are Re 1.9, 1.6, 1.4 and Im 3.8, 4.2, 2.8, so two Im ratios exceed 3. The Kummer family's ratios are 4.9–12 on the same metric (not about 20). So the planted accuracy of P1 (crossing error ≤ 1.0e-5) is not offered as the real crossing's error bar.

**Information runs** (P1 family, primary half-range per node; the 3e-12 run was added after the controls):

| noise | Re spread | Im spread | real/arc ratio | crossing error | admitted per node |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1.4e-5 | 1.6e-5 | 48–83 | 4.5e-8 | 64/70 |
| 1e-14 (the data's estimated level) | 5.7e-5–9.8e-5 | 6.6e-5–1.3e-4 | 7.5–20 | ≤ 1.8e-6 | 45–64 |
| 1e-12 (P1) | 4.1e-4–5.0e-4 | 2.7e-4–3.6e-4 | 1.4–4.2 | ≤ 1.0e-5 | 43–69 |
| 3e-12 | 6.2e-4–1.0e-3 | 6.6e-4–1.0e-3 | 0.72–2.0 | ≤ 1.3e-5 | 40–68 |
| real data | 6.9e-4–7.8e-4 | 1.0e-3–1.3e-3 | 1 | | 70/70 |

So the arc structure with about 3e-12 relative noise reproduces the real data's spread, in the pooled set and in each of qhp23/22/21. At the data's own estimated noise it does not, by 7.5–20. The real data also admits all 70 approximants at every node, while the arc family loses 6 even without noise.

A 1e-11 run was stopped by hand, because one node took 1680 s against 35 s at lower noise. Running now: `sens_noise.py` on the real data at 1e-12 and 3e-12, to see whether noise at that level costs the real data approximants too. Raw: `I214-mac/` at 5cdcd38.

**Closing summary (coordinator's subagent, mac, 2026-11-09 06:25 UTC).** Both controls pass on ten seeds, and both mutations fire. The spread does **not** match under the rule set before the runs, so the planted accuracy is not an error bar for the real crossing. The new family closes most of the gap with the data: the ratio falls from 4.9–12 for Kummer to 1.4–4.2. Information runs place the rest of the gap in the data's structure, not in its noise.

**The family** (`arc_family.py`, `fit_arc.py`, `arc_fit.json`) is a Laplace integral over a curved arc with a non-Beta density, S(x; w) = ∫₀¹ e^{x γ(s)} ρ(s) ds / ∫ρ, where γ(s) = za + s(zp − za) + κ s(1 − s) and ρ(s) = s^{α−1}(1 − s)^{β−1}(e₀ + e₁ s). Its seven complex parameters are linear in w, from one joint variable-projection fit to the three nodes. Kummer is the case κ = 0, e₁ = 0.

Fit quality, max over n = 1..22 of |log(σ_model/σ_data)|:

| w | arc | Kummer (#203) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.09 | 9.2e-5 | 8.5e-3 |
| 1.10 | 7.5e-5 | 8.7e-3 |
| 1.11 | 8.4e-5 | 8.9e-3 |

The family's own zero is exact (a series at 160 digits, which agrees with quadrature to 3e-49). It crosses at w_nat = 1.09531, with x1(1.10) = 13.50254 − 0.04904i. So σ₀..σ₂₂ at 1e-4 leave x1 free at about 0.04.

Planting is a shift in w. The σ move about 7% per 0.01 at n = 22, so the P1 family (shift −0.0003) is 2.1e-3 from the data and the P2 family (shift +0.055) is 0.36 from it.

**Controls and mutations** (criteria in `I214-mac/README.md`, raw 7b5efe0, before any control):

| check | verdict | detail |
|---|---|---|
| P1, 1.095, 1e-12 noise | pass, 10/10 | crossings 1.094990–1.094997, error ≤ 1.0e-5; \|x1 error\| ≤ 1.9e-4 |
| P2, 1.15 | pass, 10/10 | median Im x1 +0.5823, +0.4909, +0.3973 (true +0.58234, +0.49098, +0.39736); no sign change |
| M1, partial sum only | fires | no crossing; exit 0 |
| M2, crossing at 1.105 tested at 1.095 | fires | crossing 1.10500; exit 1 |

**Spread comparison.** The metric is the primary set's per-node half-range, median over seeds.

| input | Re | Im | real/planted | crossing error | admitted per node |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kummer, 1e-12 (#203) | 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-4 | 1.1e-4 to 1.7e-4 | 4.9–12 | ≤ 7.5e-6 | |
| arc, no noise | 1.4e-5 | 1.6e-5 | 48–83 | 4.5e-8 | 64/70 |
| arc, 1e-14 | 5.7e-5 to 9.8e-5 | 6.6e-5 to 1.3e-4 | 7.5–20 | ≤ 1.8e-6 | 45–64 |
| **arc, 1e-12 (P1)** | 4.1e-4 to 5.0e-4 | 2.7e-4 to 3.6e-4 | **1.4–4.2** | ≤ 1.0e-5 | 43–69 |
| arc, 3e-12 * | 6.2e-4 to 1.0e-3 | 6.6e-4 to 1.0e-3 | 0.72–2.0 | ≤ 1.3e-5 | 40–68 |
| real data | 6.9e-4 to 7.8e-4 | 1.0e-3 to 1.3e-3 | 1 | | 70/70 |
| real data + 1e-12 * | 5.4e-3 to 8.7e-3 | 1.8e-3 to 4.0e-3 | | crossing 1.09879 | 59–64 |

\* Added after the controls, for information only.

P1's Im ratios are 3.8 and 4.2 at 1.09 and 1.10, outside the rule's 1/3–3, so the spread does not match.

**What this implies for 1.09884.**
- The arc structure reaches the real data's spread only with about 3e-12 of added noise.
- The same 1e-12 noise added to the real data multiplies its spread by about 7 and costs it 6–11 approximants per node, while the clean data keeps all 70. So the real σ carry no random error near 1e-12, as the fit plateaus' 1.3e-14 says.
- The data's spread therefore comes from its structure, or from smooth errors, that no planted family here reproduces at the data's noise. Without noise the arc family is about 60× easier.
- The real crossing's stated uncertainty stays #203's envelope 1.09873–1.09894.

What each ± is:
- Every spread is a half-range over approximant choices.
- Every crossing error is |w_c − w_p| on a planted family, an estimator error under that family.
- Nothing here is a bound.

Weak support: on every planted run the crossing error was 5–20× smaller than its envelope's half-width.

**Raw:** `I214-mac/`, head 4a47ef9. **Code:** `wip/i214` 895ac75: new `fit_arc.py`, `arc_fit.json`, `arc_family.py`, `spread_compare.py`; `--family arc`, `--noise` and `--mutate_wshift` in `second_zero.py`; `--family arc` in `mutate_truncate.py`. The estimator is unchanged.

**Discrepancies and notes.**
1. #203's "about 20×" spread gap is 4.9–12× when measured as #203's primary half-range, median over its ten P1 seeds.
2. The README's first description of the P1 family's distance from the data (about 1e-4) was wrong. It is 2.1e-3, corrected in place with a note.
3. The 1e-11 run was stopped at first for slowness. The cause was the Mac's clamshell sleep from 04:03 UTC, not the noise (`exits.txt`). Later real-data noise runs were cut for the same reason.
4. A Windows commit turned the raw INDEX.md into CRLF line endings. Regenerating it here gives LF; I committed it once in the merge (2bb5b18) and later left the CRLF version alone.

**Recommended tasks**
1. *Compare #213's J 1250 − J 1500 differences with 3e-12.* What: take max |Δσ_n/σ_n|, n = 18–22, from #213. Why: it is the direct test of whether the coefficients carry errors at the level that reproduces the spread. Acceptance: if the difference is ≥ 1e-12, rerun `second_zero.py real` with it as noise and report the crossing; if it is < 1e-13, report that the spread is structural. Depends on #213 and #214.
2. *A planted family that is as hard as the data without noise.* What: richer arc families (density degree 3, cubic arc, two arcs), each fitted to ≤ 1e-5. Run `second_zero.py planted --family arc` with noise 1e-14 on them. Why: no family yet reproduces the data's noiseless spread (60× too easy), nor its 70/70 admissions. Acceptance: the real/planted spread ratio lies in 1/3–3 at every node at noise ≤ 1e-14, with ≥ 66/70 admitted, or a report that no such family was found. If one is found, its P1 crossing error is offered as the error estimate. Depends on #214.
3. *Constrained-fit planting.* What: plant the crossing by refitting the family with the constraint Im x1(w_p) = 0 instead of a w-shift. The P1 family would then stay within 1e-4 of the data rather than 2.1e-3. Acceptance: the refit P1 family's σ are within 1e-3 of the data at every node, and P1 and P2 are rerun with their verdicts. Depends on #214.

Coordinator: reviewed and merged (wip/i214 at 0b4c538; arc_family.py reproduces the fit errors 9.2e-5, 7.5e-5, 8.4e-5 and the planted offset 2.1e-3 here). Recorded in notes/HARMONY.md (df46c4a). The crossing's uncertainty stays #203's spread over approximants. Recommended tasks filed as #233 (J differences against 3e-12, after #213), #234 (a harder planted family) and #235 (constrained-fit planting).
